Question: What are some facts about Bela Lugosi, "Dracula" and/or horror movies in general?
Answer: I'll combine the first two parts of the question, by providing information on the 1931 Dracula film: According to cast member David Manners, the whole production was disorganized. No one took it seriously, except Bela Lugosi. Although Tod Browning is the credited director, it was reported that the cast received more direction from cameraman Karl Freund. It might have been that Browning was unhappy over the loss of Lon Chaney and that his enthusiasm was nil. During production, a Spanish version was planned to be shot on the same film sets. For several days, the Spanish film crew watched the English language production being made and decided they could do better. In the scene when Renfield is found laughing inside the ship of the Demeter, the voice we hear off-camera is that Tod Browning. David Manners admitted to never seeing the Dracula film and had no intention of doing so. Originally, Universal Studios planned a lavish production based largely on the Bram Stoker novel. Unfortunately with the Great Depression gripping the country, the studio had to downscale the upcoming film considerably. Like Bela Lugosi, actor Dwight Frye found himself typecast as jittery, unbalanced, eccentric characters. Bela Lugosi was the lowest paid member of the cast. He earnt $500 a week, bringing his total earnings to $3,500. Bette Davis was briefly considered for the role of Mina Seward, before Carl Laemmle decided she would be unsuitable. Thanks for reading.

Question: How were monsters made to look scary in old-timey horror movies without the use of computer-generated imagery (CGI)?
Answer: Like everything with films in those days, it was due to hard work and long hours. Lon Chaney Sr. spent much time designing various makeups, usually testing them on himself. In the long run, he had to wear glasses due to some of the chemicals used. Renown makeup artist Jack Pierce spent many hours transforming actors into monstrous beings. With Lon Chaney Jr. playing the Wolf Man, the process became tiresome. Altogether, it took approximately 21 hours to change him into a werewolf. Bits of makeup and false hair were added bits at a time, filmed and then the process was repeated. In those days, seeing really was believing. Thanks for reading.
